title: Overly broad permitAll on /auth/** in Spring Security filter chain
description: Spring Security configuration permitted all requests matching /auth/**, bypassing security filter validation for stateful endpoints such as /auth/me and /auth/switch-organization.
root_cause: Wildcard matcher /auth/** was configured with permitAll() instead of specifically allowing only public onboarding endpoints.
intended_behavior: Only explicit public endpoints (/auth/login, /auth/register-teacher, /auth/register-center, /auth/accept-invite) should be permitted without authentication.

trace.description: Wildcard matcher /auth/** permits unauthenticated requests through filter chain.
Stateful endpoint relies solely on controller null check instead of filter-level authorization.
Principal query is reached with authentication filter bypassed.

evidence.description: Wildcard permitAll allowed unauthenticated requests to reach stateful endpoints.

conditions.description: Public URL matcher used wildcard pattern /auth/** rather than exact public route paths.

execution.attacker_perspective: Unauthenticated external user sending HTTP requests.
instructions: Send GET request to /api/auth/me without providing Bearer token.
Observe that the request bypasses Spring Security filter validation and reaches controller layer.
execution.observed_result: Spring Security filter chain allows request to pass to controller without rejecting at filter boundary.

remediation.strategy: Constrain permitAll() in SecurityConfig to explicit public endpoints only, and require authentication for all other /auth endpoints.

likelihood.reason: Endpoints are directly accessible over the network.

impact.reason: Bypasses standard filter chain authentication gate, degrading defense-in-depth.

confidence.reason: Source code review confirmed wildcard matching behavior directly in SecurityConfig.

title: Missing Rate Limiting on Authentication and Roll-Call Check-in Endpoints
description: Endpoints /auth/login, /auth/register-*, and /sessions/{id}/check-in lacked rate limiting, allowing automated brute-force attacks against user credentials or roll-call QR tokens.
root_cause: No throttling or rate limiting filter was configured before the authentication provider.
intended_behavior: Public authentication and token verification routes must restrict the number of attempts allowed per IP within a sliding time window.

trace.description: Login endpoint accepts unthrottled POST requests.
Authentication manager handles unmetered authentication attempts.
Database user lookup and BCrypt verification executed repeatedly without rate throttling.

evidence.description: High-frequency credential submissions allowed without rate limit rejection.

conditions.description: External ingress or gateway does not apply strict API rate limiting.

execution.attacker_perspective: Remote adversary attempting automated password guessing or credential stuffing.
payloads: Rapid burst of 100 HTTP POST /api/auth/login attempts per second
instructions: Send multiple rapid authentication attempts with invalid credentials.
Observe application processes each request without HTTP 429 response.
execution.observed_result: Application attempts password verification for every request without throttling.

remediation.strategy: Implement an in-memory RateLimitingFilter returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests when limits are exceeded.

likelihood.reason: Automated brute-force tools are freely available and commonly used against public auth APIs.

impact.reason: May lead to credential compromise or excessive CPU utilization on password hashing.

confidence.reason: Verified that no rate limiting filters were registered in SecurityFilterChain prior to remediation.

title: Risk of CSV Formula Injection in Roster and Attendance Export
description: Student names, codes, or remarks beginning with formula trigger characters (=, +, -, @) exported into CSV could execute malicious formulas in spreadsheet applications.
root_cause: Raw unescaped strings placed directly into CSV export cells without formula character sanitization.
intended_behavior: Cells starting with formula characters must be prefixed with a single quote to force plain text interpretation.

trace.description: User-controlled student code and name fields stored in database.
Student data transformed into CSV rows.
Cell values must be sanitized to neutralize formula prefix triggers.

evidence.description: Student codes can contain characters that trigger formula execution in spreadsheet software.

conditions.description: A teacher or administrator downloads and opens the exported CSV file in spreadsheet software.

execution.attacker_perspective: Enrolled student or rogue user crafting their studentCode or name.
instructions: Register student with code starting with formula character.
Export classroom attendance report to CSV.
Open generated CSV in spreadsheet application.
execution.observed_result: Unsanitized cell interpreted as active executable formula.

remediation.strategy: Apply CsvSanitizer to prepend single quote to formula prefix characters and properly quote cells.

likelihood.reason: Requires user interaction opening the exported CSV in vulnerable desktop spreadsheet programs.

impact.reason: Could trigger unintended macro or formula execution on client workstations.

confidence.reason: Demonstrated via unit and integration tests with formula payloads.

title: Hardcoded default JWT secret in configuration without environment override
description: The default JWT secret was hardcoded in application.yml without ${JWT_SECRET:...} environment variable syntax, risking token forgery if deployed to production without configuration change.
root_cause: Missing environment variable substitution on the jwt.secret property.
intended_behavior: Secret key must be externalized to environment variables and overridden in production environments.

trace.description: Hardcoded secret string defined in repository configuration.
Constructor binds static property without requiring external secret injection.
Cryptographic HMAC signature generated using repository-tracked key.

evidence.description: Static hexadecimal secret embedded directly in version-controlled YAML.

conditions.description: Application deployed using default application.yml without external environment overrides.

execution.attacker_perspective: External adversary inspecting public source repository.
payloads: Forged JWT token signed with hardcoded secret 404E635266556A586E3272357538782F413F4428472B4B6250645367566B5970
instructions: Sign arbitrary JWT claims with role SUPER_ADMIN.
Send requests with forged Authorization header.
execution.observed_result: Backend verifies forged token successfully using the known default secret.

remediation.strategy: Externalize jwt.secret to ${JWT_SECRET:...} and enforce custom secrets in production profile.

likelihood.reason: Default secrets are easily discovered in open or leaked repositories.

impact.reason: Attacker can forge valid authentication tokens for any user or administrator.

confidence.reason: Static secret was clearly hardcoded in version control.

title: Missing Defense-in-Depth HTTP Security Headers
description: Responses lacked essential security headers (X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Strict-Transport-Security), leaving client browsers vulnerable to MIME-sniffing and clickjacking.
root_cause: Spring Security HTTP headers were not explicitly customized in SecurityFilterChain.
intended_behavior: All responses should include standard protective HTTP headers.

trace.description: HTTP security filter chain configuration omitted custom header directives.
Default filter chain builds without explicit framing or MIME constraints.
HTTP response headers emitted to client without defensive security options.

conditions.description: Upstream reverse proxy or ingress does not inject missing HTTP security headers.

execution.attacker_perspective: Web adversary embedding the application in malicious iframes or exploiting MIME sniffing.
instructions: Embed application endpoint in an external frame.
Observe absence of X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors restrictions.
execution.observed_result: Browser renders content inside external framing document.

remediation.strategy: Configure contentTypeOptions, frameOptions, and HSTS headers in Spring Security.

likelihood.reason: Requires cross-site framing or malicious content sniffing vectors.

confidence.reason: Headers were missing in initial HTTP response traces and verified in integration tests.
